body: The viola run TUI passthrough entry: the trust write sits inside the run and revive start, before the spawn, and must leave the passthrough's entry and its first screen to the child, with no viola bytes reaching the terminal.

Zero viola bytes on the terminal and the tui terminal belonging to the child: the write's outcome word goes only to the run log, never to the human's terminal, and nothing of the config file is printed anywhere.
Run diagnostics never reach the terminal: the one closed word per start is a run diagnostic carried by the run log alone.
Human keystrokes never blocked and the human taking the wheel: when the write refuses or the record is lost, the trust dialog stays the human's and viola types no key into it.
The closed word the write records per start follows the code word format, a closed list of kebab-case words with no file content or path interpolated.
Paths not carried: neither the config file's path, the folder key nor any file content appears in the closed word or any output.
Time bounds fall on the driver only: the lock wait and the at-most-3 attempts bound viola's own write, never a limit put on the human, and a lost race degrades to the human's dialog.

The write's refusals are silent degradations, not CLI refusals: a file absent, unreadable, a link, not the JSON expected or oversize, a lost race, an unverified CLI, a folder already trusted, or the home folder each leave the start to proceed with no new refusal line or exit code.

Start refusals at run and revive (home strict-modes failure, socket directory failure) keep their order and form; the trust write comes after the version gate and does not run on a start already refused.
Boundary tests sequenced on records and the boundary check never inspecting claude content: the fake agent's first screen reading trust or not is read as a signature, not by parsing screen content.
Live readings never gate: the S1 and S2 live starts are evidence under the founder's cap and gate no CI job.
A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint, and each control's timeout is named and fired; ids within 16 characters.

body: The boundary widening itself: viola now writes into the Claude CLI's own config file, against the rows that say viola writes nothing under the Claude home or into Claude's config; those rows are amended by this entry's wrap as Expected amendments, and the widening takes its Decisions Log entry, bound as ratified (R2).

What the write may touch: ONLY projects[<key>].hasTrustDialogAccepted for one folder, no other key changed, no entry removed, nothing written for the home folder, and a file never created when absent.

Where the write sits in the start: only at run and revive, after the version gate and before the spawn, only on a verified CLI as the unverified-CLI gate and the version gate's strict stamps read decide; a home whose stamp predates the 23rd ledger row reads unverified and writes no trust record.

The key and the trust reading: the key is the CLI's own (git root inside a repository, else the cwd), and trust is read as the CLI reads it — the exact key, then the parent walk to the git root or to /, so no record is written for a folder a parent already trusts.

Which file: the child's config file is <CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/.claude.json when viola's home keeps that variable for the child through config.json claude_env_keep, else the user's ~/.claude.json; viola reads that ONE environment value for that one purpose, a new environment read that owes its log entry and whose value is never logged.

The refusals, each writing nothing: the file absent, unreadable, a link, not the JSON expected (not an object, projects not an object, the entry not an object), or oversize past MAX_FRAME; the read is bounded at MAX_FRAME with the default JSON depth limit and joins the bounded product reader census.

The race (R3): take the CLI's own lock when free, replace the file atomically through the one replace helper keeping its mode, read the record back before the spawn, at most 3 attempts; the residual of a concurrent write lost in the window is accepted and named in the row.
On any refusal, skip or lost record the start goes on and the trust dialog stays the human's: viola types no byte into the dialog and the refusal never blocks the human.
The run log carries one closed code word per start from the trust record's closed code words; no path, key, file content or CLAUDE value reaches any log, error message, stderr or output.
The trust record writer guarded as it stands is reused, not duplicated: one writer serves verify's Run F and the product start, and its guards hold for both callers.

Each refusal and skip case proves nothing was written: the file's bytes unchanged, no temp sibling left, no lock left — covering absent, unreadable, link, the three wrong JSON shapes, oversize, a lost race after the 3rd attempt, an unverified CLI, a folder the exact key or a parent already trusts, and the home folder.

The e2e case reaches the write through the fake agent, which reads trust from the Claude config file, so the case FAILS when viola's write is gone; a change to the fake's screens or its trust reading puts cli_verify in the gate block, and any fake seam stays under the fake-agent feature, compiled out of release.

The live arms S1 and S2 run under the rig's private config, the child isolated from the user's config and seeded from bundle logic only, with one other project's entry as sentinel and the browser-tools key claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled seeded; the rig keys only into its own pty, the stop the standing Ctrl-C never while a dialog stands, else the no-key group kill.

The live predicates each a reading can FAIL: S1 RED when the first screen reads trust, the sentinel differs by a byte, or the written record is not exactly the one key; S2 RED when the first screen does not read trust; both RED on a missing teardown word; S1's write goes only to the rig's private config file, the founder's real ~/.claude.json read only by the mark witness.

The live screens and evidence of S1 and S2 stay local, any rig credentials copy transient and unrecorded, and a spare start is spent only on a cause a start itself showed, after its mend lands through a plan revision.

Each control's timeout named in the plan's prose and fired with that flag, ids within 16 characters, holds meaning the cases ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line, each control saying what the subject does when the guard is gone; no mutation run.

A test that waits stays under the 20 s lint bound; a test-support helper spawning an instrumented binary under a cleared environment runs it in a scratch directory; a gate entry naming an installed tool's path is checked against the host.

The write acts within the same OS user trust boundary: tampering with the Claude config file by the same user stays outside the boundary, and the strict-modes checks on viola's own home still run before the start reads its state.

body: The run and revive start sequence: the trust write sits after the version gate and before the child spawn, inside the checks viola run does before the child; revive takes the same write through the shared start, its preflight order otherwise unchanged.

The write happens only on a verified CLI: the version gate needs every relied ledger row, so a home stamped at 22 rows reads unverified now that trust-record is the 23rd relied row, and such a start writes no trust record and leaves the dialog to the human.

Trust is read the CLI's way before any write: the exact key, then the parent walk up to the git root inside a repository or to / outside one; a folder the exact key or a parent already trusts gets no record, and nothing is written for the home folder.

The written record is exactly one key, projects[<key>].hasTrustDialogAccepted, with <key> the key the CLI itself writes on an accepted dialog; no other key changes, no entry is removed, another project's entry stays byte for byte as it was.

The target file: <CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR>/.claude.json when viola's home keeps that variable for the child through claude_env_keep, else the user's ~/.claude.json; viola reads that one environment value for that one purpose, through the child environment strip and its kept list.

The race handling: take the CLI's own lock when it is free, replace the file atomically keeping its mode, read the record back before the spawn, at most 3 attempts; a record still lost after the 3rd attempt writes nothing more and leaves the dialog to the human; the residual lost concurrent write of another session is accepted and named.

The refusals write nothing and never create the file: absent, unreadable, a link, not the JSON expected (not an object, projects not an object, the entry not an object), oversize past MAX_FRAME; each gets a case proving the file's bytes unchanged, no temp sibling left and no lock left.
The skips that are no refusal each get a case proving nothing written: an unverified CLI, a folder the exact key or a parent already trusts, the home folder.
viola never types a key into the trust dialog: on any refusal, skip or lost record the dialog stays the human's; no blanket dialog approval and no emulated keypress stands in for the write.

One closed word per start in the run log naming the write's outcome, nothing of the config file anywhere (no path content, no bytes, no project keys) in logs, diagnostics or error bodies; the closed code words follow the code-word format and a new word changes a closed enum only by decision.

The e2e case over the fake agent: the fake reads its trust decision from the Claude config file given by --trust-config, so a viola run in a fresh untrusted folder shows no trust screen with the write and the trust screen without it; a change to the fake's screens or trust reading puts cli_verify in the gate block.

Tests never touch the host's real ~/.claude.json or claude sessions: every case writes into a test-owned config dir under a test-owned home, a verify-driven or stamped start tied to a test-owned home, the config seeded by the test itself.

The live starts S1 and S2 on the real claude CLI, local only and never in CI, 2.1.325 by path, under the rig's private config with one other project's entry as sentinel and claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled seeded; the rig's home gets a 23-row stamp; every byte the rig types named, the stop the Ctrl-C into the rig's pty, never while a dialog stands, else the no-key group kill.

The live predicates, each one its reading can fail: S1 red when the first screen reads trust, when the sentinel entry differs by a byte, or when the written record is not exactly the one key; S2 red when the first screen does not read trust; both red on a missing teardown word; a live reading is recorded as read, never as verification.

In S1 viola's write goes to the rig's private <scratch>/config/.claude.json; the founder's real ~/.claude.json is only read, by the mark witness; a spare start is spent only on a cause a start itself showed, after its mend lands through a plan revision.

Each control's --timeout S is named in the plan's prose and fired with that flag, on an entry whose build reaches every binary its case needs; ids within 16 characters; holds means those cases ran and failed with no TIMEOUT line; each control says what the subject does when the guard is gone, measured or marked unmeasured; no mutation run.
A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint; a test-support helper spawning an instrumented binary under a cleared environment runs it in a scratch directory and re-adds LLVM_PROFILE_FILE.
The relied ledger row trust-record, read pass live on 2.1.325, is the row the product write lands on; nothing is measured on 2.1.326 or 2.1.327 and nothing is re-pinned.
The refusal and lost-race faults are real filesystem states made by the test (a link, a chmod, an oversize file, a held lock), never a mocked filesystem; time and retries stay out of sleeps.

body_fields.convention: every new test function follows the test naming rule and its cases sit in table-driven rstest cases where they share a shape
every new test creates its own fresh home and seeds its own data; on-disk product state is produced by viola, never hand-written, and test homes are private directories
every new test waits on logged events or file state within a bound, never by sleep or retry
every new security control gets one negative test and a bounded remove-the-guard witness
every new filesystem fault in a test is a real fault on a real file, and external processes are real stub executables
every new synthetic test input carries a canary and no real data, and every new e2e assertion reads records, never the rendered child screen
every new log line is a codes-only JSON line with its schema fields, detail kept apart
